newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc option volatilites strong, others dull.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc option volatilites strong, others dull.

text.p: Zinc LME option volatilities held firm this week at the highest levels for several years, but several other metals saw volatilities stagnate as futures remained rangebound, dealers said.
Overall, the volume of business was lacklustre, they added.
Most of the zinc activity was in nearby months but some of it extended out into the third quarter, with speculative buying seen of $1,300 and $1,325 calls.
Put buying was at $1,200 and $1,225 strikes. One dealer said Far Eastern producers had been active, while another said it appeared to be short-covering.
At-the-money (ATM) implied volatility, up about one percentage point, was quoted in a wide range on Friday morning.
Dealers said April was at 23.0/27.0 percent to 26.00/30.00 percent and May at 24.5/26.0 percent to 26.0/29.0 percent.
Nickel was hit by selling as the underlying three month futures remained trapped between $7,900 and $8,100, and volatilities eased by several points.
"It may just be market makers unloading some of their long positions since the (underlying) market isn't doing anything," one trader said.
There had been sales of $8,100 straddles, strangles at $7,800/$8,200 and puts at $7,800, all for April, he added.
The sales had been well-received in the market, with good demand still seen for nickel options, the trader said.
Another trader said there had been some buying this morning of May $8,000s and $8,100s at 28.0 and 28.5 percent.
As in zinc, nickel ATM volatility quotes saw a wide range, with April said to be from 24.5/27.0 percent to 27.0/30.0 percent.
The indications on May were more uniform, within a half a point of 27.0/30.0 percent.
Copper and aluminium were dull this week, traders said.
Volatilities were barely different in copper, but they were said to be well bid.
Some buying had been seen this morning of $2,350 and $2,400 strikes with the April $2,350 going for 21.5 percent, one trader said.
There had also been interest in switching May $2,300s for $2,500s plus some players were selling ATMs for the third quarter and buying downsides, another trader said.
A third trader said producers have been enquiring for forward dates, but no business had been done.
"There has been a little bit of producer interest for min-max deals for the first half of 1998. They were interested in OTC Asian options, not TAPOS," he said.
ATM volatilities were around 20.0/22.0 percent for nearby months, descending to about 18.25/19.75 percent for December and 17.5/19.0 for first quarter 1998.
Aluminium volatilities have eased slightly after selling of April emerged on Thursday, with nearby months around 17.5/19.5 percent.
One dealer said there had been a little producer min-max activity for the average of 1998.
Lead volatilities eased a couple of points after the recent spike higher, with selling seen of $675 puts for June, which were said to be from Far Eastern trade sources.
One trader said they were trading at 29.0 percent and another said he received Aprils as low as 27.75 percent.
"Selling came in to take advantage of the higher volatilities," one said.
Tin volatilities have crept up a couple of points with speculative buying seen of nearby calls from $6,100 to $6,300. Nearby volatility was around 15.00/18.5 percent, traders said.
